core_obligations: Identify the left adjoints (proof lines 11507-11508): j'_! f'^{-1} is left adjoint to f'_*(j')^{-1}, while f^{-1}j_! is left adjoint to j^{-1}f_*.
Compare the right adjoints (proof lines 11509-11510): since f_* commutes with etale localization by construction, f'_*(j')^{-1} = j^{-1}f_*, so the two right adjoints coincide.

Conclude (proof lines 11510-11513): functors with a common right adjoint are canonically isomorphic, so j'_!f'^{-1} = f^{-1}j_! on abelian sheaves and on sheaves of modules, and the author notes this is a very general fact about morphisms of sites.
proof_roadmap: Display the two composite functors as left adjoints.
Show their right adjoints coincide using commutation of pushforward with etale localization.
Conclude the two left adjoints are equal.
Note the generality of the argument for morphisms of sites.
difficulty_reason: The lemma records that extension by zero along an etale morphism commutes with base change, j'_!f'^{-1} = f^{-1}j_! (statement lines 11492-11504). The proof is an adjointness argument: the two composite functors are identified as left adjoints of f'_*(j')^{-1} and j^{-1}f_* respectively, and commutation of pushforward with etale localization makes those right adjoints equal, so the left adjoints agree (proof lines 11507-11513). The content is the choice of adjunctions and the one identification of right adjoints. The claim is H2: a short categorical argument, with the author noting that it works for any morphism of sites.
